Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (Head of ML, Cobalt), Marcus Li (SRE), Janelle Ortiz (Product), Ravi Shah (Security), Tom Brewer (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Redwood and Cobalt aligned on POC success metrics (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on golden prompts), agreed on reporting template and runbook, next steps for sample workload delivery and benchmark kickoff, security questions noted for follow-up.

Topics covered:
- Go/no-go thresholds and pass/fail rules
- Benchmarking methodology and reporting format (CSV + summary slides)

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
00:00 Lena: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is Lena from Redwood, i'll do quick intros and then hand over to Diego for the technical acceptance criteria.
00:12 Anya: hi, yes thanks, Anya here. excited to get this scoped.
00:16 Diego: hey all, Diego Morales, infra/bench person on our side. i'll propose the benchmark schema and pass/fail rubric.
00:24 Marcus: Marcus li, SRE, i'll be running the runs and watching infra.
00:30 Janelle: Janelle, product, mostly here to confirm success metrics align to product adoption.
00:36 Ravi: ravi from security, a few compliance q's later.
00:40 Tom: Tom procurement, i'll focus on commercial parameters but listening.
00:45 Lena: great. goal today: finalize the thresholds, the format we'll use to report results, and the runbook so both teams can run the tests independently. Diego?
01:00 Diego: cool, so first slide — um, i'll talk through the measurement buckets. we propose p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (reqs per second), token cost per 1k, model quality measured against your golden set (precision/recall-ish, F1), and failure/error rates. also cold-start impact if you care.
01:20 Anya: for quality, we need both strict exact-match for criticalscenarios and a human-eval for ~200 samples. can we show both numbers? exact-match for gating and human-eval for softer guidance.
01:40 Diego: yes, exact-match will be the go/no-go.
01:44 Marcus: about traffic: our prod will be bursty. we want an at-rest baseline at 10 rps and a burst to 120 rps. can the POC simulate that, including concurrency?
02:00 Diego: yes, we can script bursts. we just need the sample payload sizes and TTL for KV — excuse me, the K-V cache warmness patterns. sometimes ASR transcribed as K-V cash in our tools.
02:16 Janelle: what about prompt length? some of our prompts are long, 1200 tokens. downsampling you'd recommend?
02:26 Diego: we will run three buckets: short (<=128 tokens), medium (<=512 tokens), long (<=1500 tokens); note that long will change the latency profile and memory residency.
02:40 Ravi: on security, KMS integration, customer-managed keys, and audit trails are mandatory for us. we need to see evidence in logs that HSM-backed keys were used or at least an integration plan.
03:00 Diego: understood. we'll include a section in the runbook to show how to wire KMS and where logs appear.
03:10 Lena: ok moving to thresholds — i'm proposing pass thresholds as follows: p95 latency <= 450ms on short, <=800ms on medium, <=1200ms on long; error rate <0.5%; exact-match on golden critical prompts >= 92%; cost per 1k tokens does not exceed the target TBD (we need your acceptable cost band).
03:40 Anya: 92% exact-match is reasonable for core set, but for some safety-critical prompts we need 98+; can we mark a small subset as hard gates?
03:56 Lena: yes, we'll allow tagging of 'hard gate' prompts, those must be >=98% exact-match or they fail.
04:06 Marcus: and if we fail a hard gate, what's remediation? do we rerun, change model variant, or is it a fail stop?
04:16 Diego: we'll define an escalation matrix: fail on hard gate triggers root-cause + optional tuning run. final decision can be go/no-go after one re-run unless otherwise agreed. we'll capture this in the runbook.
04:30 Tom: from procurement, what's the reporting cadence? weekly updates? single packet?
04:36 Lena: we'll deliver a weekly CSV + a final PDF summary with charts. Diego will attach raw logs and the benchmark spreadsheet.
04:44 Diego: spreadsheet will include columns: timestamp, model, prompt_id, token_in, token_out, p50/p95/p99, cost_token, error_flag, exact_match, human_score. we'll send a template.
04:58 Anya: can we get an example report? a one-page summary with the go/no-go call at top would be ideal.
05:06 Diego: yes, template includes a top-level pass/fail summary, and then detailed tables.
05:12 Ravi: quick security check: will redwood be storing any PII in logs? we need retention and redaction controls.
05:20 Lena: by default logs are masked; we will show how to turn on additional redaction rules and we can use customer-managed keys for any stored data. we will include AWS KMS and HSM notes in the security appendix.
05:36 Marcus: latency numbers — are these measured at the client side or service side? network jitter matters for us.
05:44 Diego: we'll report both edge-observed and server-side timings. the CSV will have both. note though, client-side includes network and is slightly noisier.
05:58 Janelle: about model variants — we may want to compare quantized vs fp16. can that be part of the run?
06:06 Diego: yes, we can run variants. we'll label rows with model_variant and quantization_flags. cost estimates will reflect those choices.
06:14 Anya: timeline? when can we kick off once you have workloads?
06:18 Lena: assuming sample workloads by 2026-01-20, Diego's team will run initial baseline within 72 hours and then schedule the full benchmark over the next week, so we aim to have a final report by 2026-01-28.
06:32 Tom: sounds fine. procurement needs trial terms; lena you'll send pilot commercial summary?
06:38 Lena: yes i'll send pilot terms and pricing bands by EOD 2026-01-17.
06:44 Diego: quick note on reporting format: we recommend CSV + an annotated Jupyter notebook for deeper dives, but we'll keep that optional.
06:56 Anya: about human eval for 200 samples — who does the labeling? our team or yours?
07:02 Diego: prefer your product team to label to avoid bias; we can provide an interface and guidelines.
07:08 Janelle: okay we'll do labeling.
07:12 Marcus: one more infra detail — are we allowed to run tests that exercise dedicated pools or will we run on hosted only?
07:20 Lena: for the POC we'll run on Redwood Hosted by default; if you want dedicated capacity we can emulate performance with similar configs but dedicated would need procurement signoff.
07:32 Marcus: understood. for the POC hosted is fine.
07:36 Ravi: any additional compliance paperwork needed? we have a checklist, we'll send it.
07:40 Lena: send it to me and i'll loop in our security team.
07:44 Diego: okay i'm going to read the proposed go/no-go rubric out loud so we're explicit:
08:00 Diego: pass if — all hard-gate prompts achieve >=98% exact-match; overall golden set >=92% exact-match; p95 latency under thresholds by bucket; error rate <0.5%; and cost per 1k tokens within agreed band. if any single hard-gate fails then the run is a fail unless tuned and re-tested.
08:26 Anya: i'm good with that. we will mark five prompts as hard-gates, list coming in the payload.
08:32 Lena: great. reporting: Diego will produce the CSV and a one-page summary that explicitly states go or no-go with the failing items called out.
08:44 Diego: we'll also attach run artifacts: logs, model config, seed prompts, and the raw inference traces.
08:52 Janelle: question: what does success look like to product? how do we translate POC pass to a pilot rollout?
08:58 Janelle: internally we'll need adoption metrics and error budgets defined; if the POC passes, we want a 6-week pilot to validate real traffic.
09:08 Lena: ok that's reasonable.
09:12 Tom: procurement question: do we have credit limits for the pilot?
09:18 Lena: yes i'll propose a pilot credit envelope in the pricing note.
09:22 Ravi: one more on logs — retention defaults to 30 days, can be extended to 90 with enterprise package?
09:30 Lena: yes that's accurate.
09:34 Diego: last technical note — we'll include warmup runs to fill KV cache and measure steady-state. call it 5 minutes warmup for long prompts.
09:44 Marcus: fine.
09:46 -- cross talk / typing --
10:10 Lena: ok let's recap next steps, i'll read out and you confirm: 1) Diego sends benchmark spreadsheet and CSV template by 2026-01-18; 2) Cobalt provides sample workloads + golden prompts and marks hard gates by 2026-01-20; 3) Redwood shows security appendix and KMS notes by 2026-01-22; 4) pilot kickoff week of 2026-01-26, final report target 2026-01-28.
10:52 Anya: acknowledged.
10:54 Marcus: ack.
10:55 Ravi: ack.
10:56 Tom: ack.
10:58 Lena: any blockers on the timeline?
11:02 Anya: only internal labeling effort which we're on track for.
11:06 Diego: i'll email the template after the call.
11:10 Lena: okay, thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
